Executive Vice President and Group Chief Financial Officer.

Ramesh Gopalan: 
Thank you, Siddharth. Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining 
us for our Q2 FY '27 earnings call. U.S. healthcare is still navigating steep 
cost increases overall. However, many of the national payers reported a 
significant improvement in their profitability in the first half of 2026 as a 
result of right sizing of membership and decrease in medical utilisation 
rates. In order to retain these margins, they need to continue to focus on 
managing medical costs, improving clinical and care outcomes, and 
driving operational efficiency. To help them achieve these objectives, 
they turn to large scale domain specialist players like Sagility, that 
combine deep healthcare expertise with AI capabilities and flexible 
partnership models, and greater accountability for outcomes. 
 
We are pleased with the progress that we have made through the first half 
of FY '27. The business momentum has been strong. We are expanding 
within our existing relationships. The clients we added in FY '26 are 
growing well, and our pipeline is robust. 
 
Let me start with what we are seeing in the market. Demand remains 
healthy, and clients are more deliberate in how they make decisions. 
Clients are prioritising investments that address immediate business 
pressures and show a clear path to measurable value. This is creating 
opportunities across our core business, managed services, and AI. For 
larger transformational deals, the buying process is more rigorous. More 
senior stakeholders are involved, and clients want a compelling business 

 
Page | 3  
case, clear evidence of value, and confidence that their partner can 
execute at scale. 
 
Increasingly, they are choosing partners who combine deep domain 
expertise with practical AI and a willingness to take accountability for 
outcomes. Our pipeline reflects the shift. It includes more managed 
service deals and a healthy set of opportunities with Blues and other mid-
market plans. This quarter, we won a large payment integrity engagement 
from a Big Ten health plan covering over 10 million members. This win 
demonstrates our growing ability to secure larger, higher value 
engagements. The deal has a minimum potential of over $10 million in 
ACV and could possibly be much more. 
 
In payment integrity deals, which are contingency-based linked to 
payment recovery, revenue will build progressively over time. Our other 
managed services deals are also progressing well. By their very nature, 
they take longer to negotiate and close, but they lead to deeper, longer- 
term relationships. AI is now central to these transformation 
conversations with clients. We are seeing this momentum translate into 
new SOW wins and more solutions moving into production. 
 
Our focus is on practical healthcare-specific solutions such as SmarTec 
Appeals Assist, Nurse Assist, and Claims Assist, which address real 
client priorities. We are gradually progressing from narrow AI use cases to 
a larger end-to-end workflow transformation using agentic AI. For 
example, for a client, we are implementing Synchrony Claims Lifecycle, 
an agentic workflow for claims adjudication, where multiple agents 
working in tandem with human in the loop handle extraction from 
unstructured inputs, drive workflows basis SOP for each scenario, do 
reasoning and decisioning, all of this in order to adjudicate a claim 
adhering to all compliance requirements. 
 
Similarly, in RCM, we are deploying Synchrony RCM Lifecycle, an agentic 
solution to handle denials, including identification, evidence collection, 
determination of appealability, and writing the appeal letters, again with 
humans reviewing at distinct checkpoints. We are also leveraging AI in 
how we go to market. It's helping us develop solutions faster, align more 
closely with client priorities, and have more strategic value focused 
conversations with clients. 
 
We are making progress on our other strategic priorities as well, 
broadening our capabilities across the healthcare value chain, and 
expanding our addressable market. The CareSeed acquisition 
announced last quarter is now integrated into our clinical practice. It

strengthens our healthcare quality capabilities, particularly in the 
Medicare Advantage market, and gives us access to a broader base of 
mid- and small-sized clients. 
 
Yesterday, we announced the acquisition of Chirok Health LLC. Providers 
are a clear growth focus for us, and Chirok fits in line with that strategy. 
Chirok's mid-cycle revenue solutions are a natural complement to 
Sagility's proven front-end and back-end revenue cycle offerings, helping 
Sagility generate improved financial and operational outcomes for health 
providers from patient access through final payment. I will talk about 
Chirok a little more in detail later. Along with this, we are also scaling our 
provider go-to-market team to accelerate growth in the provider segment. 
 
With this, let me get into the specifics of our Q2 and H1 performance. 
Consolidated revenue for Q2 came in at INR 20,321 million, or $212.6 
million, representing a year-on-year growth of 22.5% in INR terms and 
12.2% in constant currency. Excluding the CareSeed acquisition, organic 
revenue growth remains strong at 22.2% in INR terms and 11.9% in 
constant currency. 
 
Operating profitability remains strong with Q2 adjusted EBITDA at INR 
5,353 million, or $56 million, representing a year-on-year growth of 23%, 
with a margin of 26.3%, the highest in six quarters. Net profitability also 
remained healthy. Adjusted PAT for Q2 was INR 3,254 million, or $34 
million, up 8.1% year-on-year, with a margin of 16%. 
 
Turning to the half year performance. H1 FY '27 was INR 39,956 million, or 
$420.4 million, representing on a year-on-year growth of 25% in INR terms 
and 13.7% in constant currency. H1 adjusted EBITDA was INR 10,069 
million, or $105.9 million, growing 25.2% year-on-year with a margin of 
25.2%, while adjusted PAT was INR 5,951 million, or $62.6 million, 
growing 18.9% year-on-year with a margin of 14.9%. 
 
Moving to new deal wins, deal ACV increased 18.2% year-on-year to $40.2 
million, with wins across 31 existing clients and one new client. I am also 
happy to announce that the board has approved an interim dividend of 
INR 0.15 or 15 paise per share to be paid in Q3. Before I move on, I'd like 
to highlight some of the external recognition we received this quarter. 
Industry analysts are increasingly recognizing our healthcare depth and 
our ability to deliver transformation at scale. Sagility received the 2026 
Everest Group Elevate Honor for Voice of the Customer in the Healthcare 
and Life Sciences Service Specialist category.

research and recognize top performing service providers based on direct 
client feedback. In addition to this, Avasant named us as leader in the 
healthcare payer business process transformation. Our SmarTec Nurse 
Assist Solution won a Stratus Awards for Cloud Computing. On the 
people front, Sagility ranked 57th in the 100 Best Large Workplaces in Asia 
2026 by Great Place to Work, and we were also recognized amongst the 
Top 10 India's Best Places for Women in 2026. Sagility also earned its 
Great Place to Work certification for a second year in a row. We also won 
a Bronze Stevie Award for AI adoption with headcount growth in the U.S.

for ESG, which recognises our commitment to responsible business 
practices. Together, these awards recognise our healthcare expertise, 
our progress on AI, and the culture of doing right for all stakeholders that 
our teams have built.
